script.title: Composite vs Mixed Supply under CGST
script.caption_hook: One price for everything: is it always a mixed supply?

lines.say: Ma'am, everything's sold for one price. Is that always a mixed supply?
Not always. First ask: are the items naturally bundled?
Goods packed, transported and insured together, in the ordinary course of business. That's a composite supply.
So which one decides the tax?
The goods are the principal supply. Section 8(a): tax the whole supply as the principal supply.

board.title: Section 8(a)
board.sub: Taxed at the rate of the principal supply

lines.say: A gift box: chocolates, dry fruits, a soft toy, one price. Not natural, single price: mixed.
Then which rate applies to the gift box?
Section 8(b): tax it as the supply with the highest rate of tax.

board.title: Section 8(b)
board.sub: Whole box taxed at the highest rate

lines.say: So a single price alone doesn't decide it!
Right. A single price alone doesn't make it mixed. Check for a natural bundle first; if not, and one price, it's mixed.
Remember: natural bundle, taxed as the principal supply. Otherwise, single price, taxed at the highest rate.
